obligations.definition: DADD uses old C as the carry-in for the least significant group and adds S/D in 4-bit groups from low to high. Each group first forms a 5-bit sum; if it is less than 10, retain it, otherwise add 6 within 5 bits. Result bit4 propagates to the next group; concatenate the low 4 bits of each group, with bit4 of the final group becoming bit16. All nibbles, including a through f, are legal; 5-bit arithmetic overflow is truncated; in byte execution, the low-byte carry can still reach bit8. DADD is not further gated directly by jump or exec.
obligations.setup: Combinational inputs, with no preparation state; all are driven to known legal values, with special four-state cases governed by the provisions
obligations.stimulus: Each vector explicitly drives all native inputs to known two-state values; items not listed herein are fixed at 0, with no dependence on reset or historical preparation. In the main loop, exec_cycle=1 and inst_bw=0; only inst_alu[7]=1 selects DADD, while ADD, halt, and IRQ are all 0, and jump=0. For each target 4-bit group, iterate S/D nibbles from 0 through f and old C=0/1; set S/D above the target group to 0, and set S=9 and D=0 in all lower groups so that old C propagates group by group to the target group. Word mode covers all four groups; additionally cross exec_cycle and inst_bw, testing 9999+0001, ffff+ffff, and 0099+0001, including non-BCD nibbles and byte bit8 carry. Then set inst_jmp=3, old Z=0/1, old C=1, src=2, and dst=3, retain DADD, and cross exec=0/1 to confirm that a failed jump does not gate the DADD output. Each vector is held for 10ns and sampled at 2ns/8ns.

obligations.definition: AND/OR/XOR use S/D; SWPB swaps the two bytes of the original op_src, and SXT extends the low byte according to the original op_src[7]. SHIFT shifts the original source right by one bit, filling bit15 with RRC?old C:(inst_bw?original bit7:original bit15); in byte mode, bit7 is also filled with this value, bit14:8 comes from original bit15:9, and bit6:0 comes from original bit7:1. The selected AND/OR/XOR/SHIFT/SWPB/SXT results are bitwise ORed; S passes through only when none is selected. IRQ or halt or ADD takes priority in selecting the base addition plus increment, followed by DADD, and finally the short paths; data priority does not change status selection bits.
